Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The information age has brought advancements in technology and data collection techniques that produce an abundance of accessible data in all sectors and created a new paradigm for science, based on data-intensive computing.
The ever-increasing data is often unstructured and requires development of new techniques for storage, analysis, and effective decision making.
Data science is the study of complex data or big data.
It involves developing methods to collect, record, store, analyze, and interpret data to effectively extract useful information and detect patterns, trends, and relationships in data sets for decision-making purposes.
The data scientist is often a storyteller presenting data insights to decision makers in a way that is understandable and applicable to their interests.

2 The field of data science, including data mining and machine learning, is interdisciplinary at its core, drawing upon skills in computer science, mathematics, statistics, and ethics.
Its primary goal is to gain insights and knowledge from any type of data, both structured and unstructured, and provide important resources to organizations that make data-driven decisions.
As new technologies are developed, data science will continue to grow in importance to business, industry, science, many academic disciplines, healthcare, and government in the years ahead.
Data scientists are employed in many settings, including finance & insurance, professional services, healthcare & social assistance, retail trade, and manufacturing.
Top industries hiring data scientists: Information Technology & Services, Computer Software, Internet, Financial Services, and Higher Education.
Although Hanover’s Market Opportunity Scan: National Degree Programs (Updated), prepared for URI in July 2018, does not explicitly address programs in data science, it does address the potential for a graduate certificate in Artificial Intelligence, which is closely related to machine learning, a core subject of data science.

The market analysis suggests using the development of such a graduate certificate as "a vehicle for career advancement that requires less time and resources than a master’s degree.” Furthermore, the analysis suggests that "the labor market demand for artificial intelligence professionals is strong, and that related fields (including computer and information research science and software development) are projected to add 121,000 jobs per year between 2016 and 2026.” Indeed, not many online certificate programs in artificial intelligence exist today outside of one at Johns Hopkins and one at Stanford.
Regarding data science, Lewis University has an online Graduate Certificate in Data Science and Cornell has an online Graduate Certificate in Data Analytics, which has a business focus.
Today, the job prospects for Data Scientists are strong.
Currently, of the approximately 134,000 open job announcements for data science or data scientist listed on Indeed.com, approximately 1,700 are entry level positions.

Since its inception five years ago, Glassdoor ranked Data Scientist as one of the top 10 best jobs in America, based on median base salary, the number of active job openings, and employee satisfaction rates, with a #1 ranking in 2016, 2017, and 2018.
LinkedIn’s 2020 Emerging Jobs Report ranks Data Scientist as #3 in the list of Top 15 Emerging Jobs in the U.S.
The report states, “It’s a specialty that’s continuing to grow significantly across all industries.
Our data indicates some of this growth can likely be attributed to the evolution of previously existing jobs, like statisticians, and increased emphasis on data in academic research.” Robert Half Technology, a search firm, produced the Salary Guide 2020, in which they list salaries for Data Scientists between $105K and $180K, depending on the geographical location, experience, and expertise of the employee.
They state that “upskilling” is a priority for most IT departments as they grow skill sets in-house.
After conducting a survey, they found that 90% of technology managers are upskilling some of their employees.
Data science and machine learning are among the most common areas for professional development.

Companies upskilling in-house employees represent a potential market for this program, as they may fund their employees to enroll in this program as part of their professional development.
The time is right.
With the growth in jobs, will come learner demand and URI will have one of the first Online graduate certificate programs in data science offered by an accredited university.
This certificate, as is suggested in the Hanover report, will be marketed as a “vehicle for career advancement that requires less time and resources than a master’s degree.” There are many reasons why someone might seek a certificate in data science.
One may be looking to switch to a more lucrative career or improve their skills to achieve a higher level within their profession.
With job prospects decreasing in some areas, adding data science skills could greatly enhance career opportunities.
One may even wish to pursue a master’s degree but get started with a certificate that is more quickly obtainable.

This program targets professionals seeking recent data analysis methods and technologies that could be applied into their current work roles; recent graduates (including those from URI) that are looking to expand their skills and land into data science related jobs; recent graduates who are interested in graduate programs in data science and related fields; students interested in data visualization to develop and communicate insights about the data; professionals who need data science skills to contribute to other fields; and current students in graduate programs seeking skills in data science to apply to their discipline.

3 This program is offered in the accelerated 7-week calendar format, a delivery method that provides flexibility to domestic and international students, working professionals, and active and reserve service members.
It complements URI’s undergraduate Data Science Program.
A master’s degree program in data science is being planned and this program is designed so that the credits earned from this program will partially satisfy the requirements of the master’s degree.
The Program’s main objectives are to 1) prepare students for careers in data-driven industries and sciences, 2) provide students who have domain area knowledge with the skill set to solve data-driven problems, and 3) prepare students for further graduate studies.

After completion of this Graduate Certificate program, students will have the ability to: ● work with large scale datasets from the perspective of database structures and storage ● manipulate and prepare data for program analysis ● identify and use the correct statistical methodology to solve real data-driven problems ● form data-driven questions and conduct analysis using perspectives of computer science, machine learning, statistics, and mathematics ● recognize the ethical implications of data on individuals and society ● extract insights from data through state-of-the-art data visualization techniques ● go beyond the data and the software to effectively communicate to non-technical audience ● synthesize knowledge and categorize data from various sources to solve problems in various fields ● use computational skills in interdisciplinary teams to solve problems in data-driven domains ● program in Java, R, Python, and SQL Students complete a research project in a domain area of their choice.

This program prepares data scientists to excel in machine learning, management, analysis of large and/or unruly datasets, and visualization through an approach that privileges problem solving and collaborative research.
We expect 50-70 unique students to enroll in the certificate program each year, entering during any one of the six 7-week sessions.
Applicants will be expected to provide 1) college transcripts certifying successful completion of a Bachelor’s degree 2) two letters of recommendation from peers, mentors, or colleagues attesting to the student’s ability to complete graduate level coursework, and 3) a personal written statement explaining why the student is seeking a University of Rhode Island Online Graduate Certificate in Data Science.
One needs to have prior education in calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, programming in Python.
Students may be admitted under provisional status, followed by full admission once they complete the missing prerequisites.
Pre-requests may be completed at URI or at another institution, including open source courseware.
Accepted students will complete a sequence of five 3-credit classes for a total of 15 credits.

They may take one course each 7-week session and complete the program in less than one year.
Since this is an online program, the expectation is that it will be funded through revenues generated by the program itself and no other revenue will be needed.
